impact: The Rootly Agent handed 27.6% of web asks back to the user (vs 9.0% in Slack) across 914 of 3,165 paying-team users from Aug 2 to Nov 12, with no outage.

scope.users: 3,165 users asked the agent; 914 (29%) on 205 teams were handed back at least once; 208 users hit the same intent wall 2+ times
scope.slo: not applicable: product sizing, not an availability or latency SLO

executive_summary: The data pack is published at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/5703be40-69c9-43c3-bd5d-c303fa9781a8 (private until shared). Window: the last 6 months of sessions (about 150k since May); message text exists only from Aug 2, so ask-level numbers cover Aug 2 - Nov 12. Of 21,810 asks, the agent replied without refusing to 89.8% (Tier 1, an upper bound because there is no resolution feedback), pointed to docs for 0.76% (Tier 2) and handed back 9.4% (Tier 3). Web, where the homepage will live, hands back 27.6% because web chat lacks incident-update, paging and retro tools. Handbacks are broad, not a few accounts: 914 of 3,165 users, and the top 10 teams' rate (9.3%) matches the rest (9.5%). But 208 users were handed back on the same intent repeatedly (46% of handbacks). Braintrust metadata shows the golden-set eval (38 scenarios, 894 cases) is organized by tool and has no cases for 7 intents that hold 24% of handbacks: Slack channel, declare, tickets, config, metrics, root cause and shift cover. Scores and traces stay blocked by the lane hook. Proposed KR: at least 85% resolved by a real resolution signal; config and admin asks routed to Tier 2; at most 9% handed back on the homepage with a 5% stretch, measured offline by adding persona and surface scenarios to the golden set.
root_cause: Web chat offers most users only read-only tools and the golden-set eval has no cases for the intents handed back most, so web returns incident-update, paging and retro asks that Slack completes and nothing offline shows it.
trigger: No incident trigger: the homepage redesign kickoff asked for data to size a 3-tier KR before the agent moves from the incident page to a global component.
detection: Measured on request with text rules over ai_session_messages; there is no structured refusal tag or resolution feedback, so no dashboard tracks tier rates today.
resolution: Data pack published; the KR targets and the web write-tool scope are product decisions still to make.
five_whys: More than one in four web asks to the agent ends with the work handed back to the user.
Web chat refuses incident updates, paging and retros that Slack completes.
Web chat keeps only READ_ONLY_TOOLS unless the user passes home-chat gating, and even then it has no incident-update, paging or retro tool.
Write access on web was scoped to the early home-chat rollout and never extended to incident-level actions.
The scope of web write tools and the eval coverage for the global agent are product decisions the homepage redesign has to make now.

went_well: Main DB had enough to size every tier, split by surface, cluster intents, check the PRD's prompts and rank manual actions.
Checking the shape of assistant messages caught that 70% are tool-call rows, which corrected Tier 3 from 5.3% to 9.3% before the numbers reached the PRD.
The per-user split showed handbacks track volume, not specific accounts, which rules out a few customers as the cause.
went_wrong: The lane first narrowed to refusals and delivered no artifact, then shipped tier numbers that paired asks with tool-call rows; both needed rework.
Braintrust trace and score reads stayed blocked by the hook; only experiment metadata could be used.
Feedback is empty, so Tier 1 is only an upper bound.
Message text is stored only from Aug 2, so the requested 6-month view of asks covers 14 weeks.
got_lucky: Home chat has almost no volume yet (about 67 sessions), so the web read-only gap has not hit homepage users at scale.
If the 90-day window had covered only Sep 21 to Oct 11, Tier 3 would have read about 4% and the KR target would have been set too low.

summary: Third rework, following operator guidance (Braintrust findings, per-user distribution, 6-month intent breakdown with handback rates, JJ's methodology). (1) Window moved to 180 days. Sessions go back to May, but message text starts Aug 2, so asks cover Aug 2 - Nov 12. Numbers barely move: 21,810 asks, Tier 3 9.4%, web 27.6%, Slack 9.0%. (2) Per-user (h7, invalidated): handbacks are broad (914 of 3,165 users, 205 teams, and the top 10 teams' rate matches the rest), with a repeat tail (208 users, 46% of handbacks). (3) Intent x month heatmap added: declare and paging improved from Aug to Oct; Slack channel, retro and tickets stayed high. (4) Braintrust (h8, validated): the golden-set eval (38 scenarios, 894 cases, env:test) is tool-organized and has no cases for 7 intents holding 24% of handbacks. rootly-prod-agent was created Sep 18, a lead for the Sep 21 dip. Scores and traces stay blocked by the hook. (5) JJ's methodology answered on the page: real asks replace incident mining; the golden set is the harness for persona prompts; repeat handbacks seed the hard set. KPI mapping included. The new artifact URL replaces the old one because the lane hook refused updates to the earlier artifact after the session reset. h2 stays the mechanism; h6 leads. Caveats: keyword intents, about 80% refusal precision, intent-to-scenario mapping by name.
